headline: India Surges in Solar Manufacturing, Adding 50.6 GW in First Half of 2026
meta_description: India expanded solar module manufacturing by 50.6 GW in early 2026, reaching 261.7 GW cumulative capacity and strengthening its clean energy infrastructure.
summary_short: India added 50.6 GW of solar module manufacturing capacity in the first half of 2026, bringing its total to 261.7 GW and advancing clean energy production.
body:
India added 50.6 gigawatts of solar module manufacturing capacity in the first half of 2026, pushing its cumulative solar module manufacturing capacity to 261.7 GW.

The country also expanded cell manufacturing capacity by 9.7 GW during the same period. These figures reflect India's accelerating commitment to becoming a major player in renewable energy production, moving beyond simply installing solar systems to building the domestic infrastructure that manufactures the components themselves.

This growth matters because manufacturing capacity translates to jobs, energy independence, and a stronger position in the global clean energy supply chain. India's rapid expansion shows how quickly a nation can scale production when clean energy becomes a priority.
quick_facts: India added 50.6 GW of solar module capacity in 1H 2026
Total cumulative solar module capacity reached 261.7 GW
Cell manufacturing capacity increased by 9.7 GW
